fields.v: Zhejiang University, Hangzhou (Liu S., Zhao, Hu, Yang, Xia); Hangzhou High-Tech Zone (Binjiang) Institute of Blockchain and Data Security (Xia); independent researcher, Shanghai (Liu K.)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — RACE-Bench (528 feature-addition instances with structured reference reasoning) and a dual-track evaluation (patch correctness + reasoning alignment); evaluation of three code agents with up to three base LLMs
No SDD approach. Agents compared: AutoCodeRover, TraeAgent, mini-SWE-Agent (versions Not stated; default configurations); base LLMs DeepSeek V3.2, GLM-4.7, GPT-5.2

N/A for the agents. Benchmark instance: Feature Request (from GitHub issue) and Fail-to-Pass tests given to the agent as 'executable specification'; hidden Pass-to-Pass tests; Reference Reasoning (concept explanations, goal expectation, file localization, specific tasks, task steps); gold and test patches; optional hints text

Reference reasoning schema: issue understanding -> file localization -> issue implementation (specific tasks) -> step decomposition. Evaluation: agent inputs -> agent execution (reasoning-action loop) -> dual-track evaluation (patch verification; reasoning summarized by LLM and compared with reference)
None in the agent runs. Benchmark construction: manual check of 100 intent labels, manual recheck of feature-addition candidates; two authors inspect 100 audited instances and 100 evaluated runs
Full agent workflow on single feature-addition tasks; case study adds a file-localization stage to TraeAgent
Not classifiable (agent benchmark; FTP tests called an 'executable specification'; no SDD terms)
Existing code bases: feature addition from real GitHub issues/PRs
528 instances from 12 repositories (14,333 PRs -> 2,931 -> 580 -> 528); RACE-Bench Lite 100 instances; instance size not reported beyond examples
The 12 popular open-source Python repositories of SWE-bench (e.g. astropy, xarray, sympy, pytest)

Reasoning alignment with the reference: Recall@Concept, Accuracy@Concept, Score@GoalExpectation (10-point LLM judge), Recall and OverPrediction at Files, SpecificTasks and TaskSteps; FTP coverage of feature requests; implementation diversity of successful patches

Automatic: pytest FTP/PTP execution in per-instance Docker; agent traces normalized by a summarizer LLM (DeepSeek V3.2, temperature 0) and enriched by patch back-inference; deterministic plus LLM-as-judge matching (DeepSeek). Manual: two authors validated 100 evaluated runs (97/100 agreement); GPT-5.5 classifications in Section 5.1 not human-validated

Criterion: FTP and PTP tests per instance; no success criterion for a configuration stated by the authors. Full RACE-Bench (528), DeepSeek V3.2, single run: (a) AutoCodeRover + DeepSeek V3.2: Apply 96.21%, Resolved 28.79%; Recall Files/Tasks/Steps 0.840/0.675/0.397, OverPred 0.067/0.255/0.579. (b) TraeAgent + DeepSeek V3.2: Apply 78.98%, Resolved 52.65%; Recall 0.746/0.607/0.340, OverPred 0.420/0.334/0.652. (c) mini-SWE-Agent + DeepSeek V3.2: Apply 95.83%, Resolved 70.08%; Recall 0.890/0.751/0.445, OverPred 0.049/0.208/0.584. RACE-Bench Lite (100), Resolved/Apply: (d) AutoCodeRover + DeepSeek 0.290/0.960; (e) AutoCodeRover + GLM-4.7 0.190/0.960; (f) AutoCodeRover + GPT-5.2 0.370/0.990; (g) TraeAgent + DeepSeek 0.520/0.800; (h) TraeAgent + GLM-4.7 0.720/0.920; (i) TraeAgent + GPT-5.2 0.770/0.900; (j) mini-SWE-Agent + DeepSeek 0.710/0.970; (k) mini-SWE-Agent + GLM-4.7 0.790/0.990; (l) mini-SWE-Agent + GPT-5.2 0.710/0.990. Case study (ablation): (m) TraeAgent + DeepSeek with added file-localization stage, 16 localization-failure cases: Recall@Files 0.496 -> 0.565, perfect localization 0% -> 18.8%, 4 more resolved; regressions on some of 10 previously successful cases. For each: quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors (no cost reported)

Tasks: 528 RACE-Bench instances (full) and 100 Lite instances chosen by difficulty-preserving local search from the full-benchmark runs. Configurations: 3 agents x DeepSeek V3.2 (full); 3 agents x 3 LLMs (Lite). Baseline: none beyond alternatives. Held constant: instance Docker, default agent configurations, temperature 0, top_p 1, max generation 4,096 tokens, same inputs (feature request + FTP tests), same hardware. Acceptance tests: FTP and hidden PTP tests. Repetitions: single run per instance. Human intervention: none

mini-SWE-Agent best on full benchmark (Resolved 70.08%), TraeAgent 52.65%, AutoCodeRover 28.79%; TraeAgent limited by apply failures (tool hangs). All agents high Score@Goal (9.25-9.51) but recall falls from files to tasks to steps; apply-success but test-fail patches have 35.7% lower recall and 94.1% higher over-prediction than successful ones. Lite: base LLM effect depends on agent (AutoCodeRover 0.19-0.37, TraeAgent 0.52-0.77, mini-SWE-Agent 0.71-0.79). No significance tests

Distinguished agents (29-70% resolved) and diagnosed reasoning stages; automatic reasoning evaluation agreed with authors in 97/100 runs; case study showed the signal can guide an agent change. Repeatability not assessed (single run, temperature 0). Limitations stated: single run, LLM-as-judge bias, LLM-assisted references, limited agents/models, only explicit reasoning observable, agents expose reasoning differently

Threats: LLM-as-judge bias; LLM-assisted reference reasoning may be inaccurate; Section 5.1 LLM classifications not human-validated; single run per instance; limited agents and base models; only explicit reasoning observable; differing reasoning exposure across agents. Reference reasoning is one accepted trajectory, not the only valid solution; 5.5% of FTP tests insufficiently cover the request. Gaps: agents weak at translating intent into concrete steps; model and agent design should be studied jointly

Values from Tables 2-4 (pp. 7-9). Table 4 reasoning metrics are for the Failure (excl. apply-fail) group only. TraeAgent + GPT OverPred@Files reported as 0.000 (p. 9), an extreme value not explained. Contributions claim differences in 'efficiency' but no efficiency metric is reported. Lite subset is selected using the same agents' full-benchmark results. Replication package: doi:10.5281/zenodo.19221764. No pre-registration. Programming language: Python
